questions.stem: In a pictogram, each symbol represents 8 people. How many people do 3.5 symbols represent?
What is the key difference between a bar chart and a histogram?

options.text: Bar charts have gaps between bars; histograms do not
Histograms only show qualitative data
There is no difference
Bar charts have taller bars

questions.explanation: Bar charts have gaps between bars (for discrete/categorical data), while histograms have no gaps (for continuous data). Also, histogram y-axis shows frequency density.

questions.stem: Why must the vertical axis of a bar chart start at zero?

options.text: It doesn't have to start at zero
Because it makes the chart look bigger
Because negative frequencies don't exist
To avoid exaggerating differences between bar heights

questions.explanation: Starting above zero makes small differences look much larger than they really are, giving a misleading visual impression.

questions.stem: A dual bar chart is used to:

options.text: Stack categories on top of each other
Show data for one category only
Compare two sets of data side by side
Display continuous data

questions.explanation: A dual (comparative) bar chart shows two sets of data side by side, making it easy to compare them across categories.

questions.stem: A pictogram needs to show a frequency of 14 with a key of '1 symbol = 4 people'. How many symbols are needed?

options.text: 3 full symbols and a quarter symbol
3 full symbols
3 full symbols and a half symbol
4 full symbols

questions.explanation: $14 \div 4 = 3.5$ symbols, which is 3 full symbols and one half symbol.

questions.stem: Which type of data is NOT suitable for a bar chart?

options.text: Precise weights of 1000 parcels
Favourite colours of students
Number of pets owned
Types of transport used

questions.explanation: Precise weights of many parcels are continuous data with a wide range, better suited to a histogram. Bar charts work well for categorical or discrete data.

questions.stem: In a bar chart, the bars should be:

options.text: Touching with no gaps
Arranged in descending order of height
The same width with equal gaps between them
Different widths to represent different values

questions.explanation: Bar chart bars should all be the same width with equal gaps between them. This ensures that only the height represents the frequency.
